reviewed.v1_status: Superseded draft; not reviewed for release

positive_static_findings: Reachable runner --run and gate --preflight/--execute remain hard rc3. Current CLI cannot SSH or execute graph; no reachable Docker/Podman/OCI, namespace, chroot or mount route was found.

Dormant evaluate/preflight_once can write one atomic link-created EVO19-GATE.json containing expected local env/wrapper, intended argv/interpreter, expected and observed remote input SHA/size/mode, plus separate outer SSH and remote readback rc. Nine injected local fixtures match their persisted hashes and cover success, mismatch, SSH failure, env failure, receipt path mismatch and no replacement; they do not perform SSH.

Remote probe opens final file components O_NOFOLLOW and reads each file through one fd; local wrapper identity is also fd-based. This is stronger than the v5 ad hoc hash checks but remains an observation, not execution-byte pinning.

blocking_findings.finding: The authoritative local_env parse is used to check config SHA and host only; remote runner/interpreter/input paths are supplied by an external spec without derivation from the frozen NANHAI bindings or exact reviewed runner SHA. A local validation-only counterexample with runner /tmp/arbitrary-runner.py and remote_interpreter /usr/bin/python3; false # passed validate_spec. The latter is placed directly in the SSH remote-command argument position. A future release must fix the interpreter to a reviewed literal and derive/validate every path and digest against the accepted environment and runner packet before any SSH call. No malicious SSH was attempted.

Local/remote stability tuples compare dev, inode, size and mtime, not mode or ctime; chmod during read can leave the reported pre-read mode and stable=true. O_NOFOLLOW protects only the final component, not mutable parent symlinks. The probe closes its fd before any future graph command and has no immutable staged executable handoff or execution-time recheck, so a passing receipt does not bind bytes actually executed.

The spec accepts any absolute path ending EVO19-GATE.json; it does not constrain the receipt to the project-owned control directory. If the destination parent is absent/unwritable, the function returns FAIL_CLOSED_NO_VALID_RECEIPT without a durable receipt. If the hard link succeeds but directory fsync fails, a PASS file may remain while the caller reports write failure. The release consumer must require a fixed project receipt location, parseable matching digest and successful outer terminal receipt before trusting PASS.

No exact release spec, original-owner graph ACK, actual gz02 readback, or dispatch exists for this SHA. The receipt status is explicitly PREFLIGHT_PASS_ONLY_NOT_GRAPH_RELEASE; outer_ssh_rc and remote_rc refer to input readback, not the graph runner's terminal rc. Real Linux descendant cleanup, inherited seccomp/complete trace, source guards and Soong graph artifacts remain unproven.

adversarial_local_check.action: Import exact gate module and call validate_spec only, with synthetic required input rows and wrapper; no transport call.
adversarial_local_check.result: Accepted arbitrary /tmp/arbitrary-runner.py and remote interpreter string /usr/bin/python3; false # while constructing intended argv [interpreter,-B,runner,--run].

minimum_next: Keep all execution routes rc3. First make the preflight SSH command literal and constrain spec paths/receipt destination to accepted local_env/project bindings and exact reviewed runner/wrapper identity. Add mode/ctime and parent-chain checks, then design an execution-time immutable handoff or immediate recheck. Re-review new bytes and fixtures before any actual SSH readback; graph release additionally needs original-owner ACK and actual runtime safety evidence.
peer_actions: Static source/diff/receipt review and one local validate_spec-only counterexample. No SSH, graph, container, namespace, chroot, mount, device or Bridge action.
